reason: A premise's scope prose was corrected where a deletion left it naming a unit that no longer exists, and THM-0074's theorem_dependencies digest moved with it. Exactly one of THM-0074's component entries differs from origin/main -- theorem_dependencies[THM-0023], sha256:5e77ea10 -> sha256:f64459a6 -- and every other premise, the encoding version and the root's own claim digest are identical. This is the third instance of one shape: a root's fingerprint is sensitive to prose throughout its closure, so retiring a unit obliges every sentence in that closure which named it to stop naming it. The correction was also checked in the strengthening direction, and that check found a defect: an intermediate cohort state had replaced the clause with a positive universal over all callers, which would have been STRONGER than the reviewed text at the moment the only caller-side edge was deleted. That was corrected at 225d77a4 before this measurement, and the text recorded here is weaker than both.
ruling: ADR-MCPRE-068 Phase-1 campaign ruling, 2026-09-18, item 5: claim precision corrections that preserve the ratified promise, and moving evidence to its correct owner, are explicitly NOT owner escalations. The owner did not individually review this fingerprint; the authority recorded here is that ruling. No root statement, security_consequence or scope is edited -- THM-0074's own theorem_claim digest is sha256:9f4cc66a on both sides of this transition, as it was on both sides of the two records before it. The movement is entirely in theorem_dependencies, inherited from one premise whose scope prose named a unit this branch deletes.
